newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Embratel to invest over 900 mln reais in 97.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Embratel to invest over 900 mln reais in 97.

text.p: Brazil's state long-distance telecoms firm Embratel plans to invest between 900 million reais and one billion reais in 1997, up from this year's total spending plan of 850 million reais, an official said.

An Embratel spokeswoman told Reuters that this year's plans called for spending roughly 500 million reais to expand national fiber optic lines, a new traffic central and its B3 satellite, slated for launching in late 1998.
A total of 326 million reais is to be spent this year, and 544 million reais next year on Embratel's existing network, said the spokeswoman, who asked not to be named.
She did not give details for the rest of next year's spending plan, except to say that the firm expected total investment to reach just under one billion reais.
Meanwhile, a local newspaper said Embratel posted a net profit of 305.6 million reais in the first eight months, up 116 percent from the same period last year.
Gazeta Mercantil, quoting company President Dilio Penedo, said Embratel had net earnings of 141.9 million reais in January-August 1995.
Company spokesmen said they could not immediately confirm the figures.
The paper said the firm showed an operating profit of 392.3 million reais in the January-August period, up 650 percent from the 52 million reais reported in the same eight months last year.
It also said Embratel had net revenues of 1.239 billion reais compared with 820 million reais in the same period in 1995, while operational expenses stayed about the same.

The paper quoted Penedo as saying the main reason for the increase was a 55 percent hike in national and international long-distance call traffic, a 20-percent hike in rates for calls between Brazilian cities and a cap on expenses.
Embratel, like the 27 other subsidiaries of Brazilian telecoms giant Telebras, is expected to be privatized in the coming years.
The company, which provides national and international long-distance service, is not publically traded.
